name: Vietnam
research_note: Only 3 of the planned ~10 searches ran: the session-wide WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted mid-batch. Everything below is from those 3 result sets plus docs/SOURCES.md. The Wikipedia probes and the secondary-route checks were NOT run and are listed under searches_run as refused.

nso.name: National Statistics Office of Viet Nam (NSO; the General Statistics Office, GSO, restructured in 2025)
nso.note: Host of the search-result URL https://www.nso.gov.vn/en/events/2019/12/press-release-on-results-of-the-population-and-housing-census-01-4-2019/ . Legacy www.gso.gov.vn URLs still serve the 2019 and 2024 publications (both surfaced). docs/SOURCES.md records that gso.gov.vn times out and nso.gov.vn resets the connection from the project's runner; UNFPA co-publishes the 2019 English results volume.

latest_census.notes: 2019 Population and Housing Census, reference 1 April 2019; 96,208,984 people (press release, results published 19 Dec 2019). Ethnicity and religion are both asked (questionnaire Q6/Q7, per docs/SOURCES.md) and both are published NATIONALLY: Kinh 85.3%, 53 minorities 14.7%; six minorities over 1 million (Tay 1.85M, Thai 1.82M, Muong 1.45M, Mong 1.39M, Khmer 1.32M, Nung 1.08M); Catholic 5.9M (6.1% of population), Buddhist 4.6M (4.8%), 16 religions tabulated by sex. Whether a language question was asked was not established this session (null). A mid-decade Population and Housing Survey (Dieu tra dan so va nha o giua ky, reference 1 April 2024; 101,112,656 people; all 63 provinces except 4 island districts; sample-based) published results Dec 2024 / Jan 2025 -- the search snippet lists population size/structure, marital status, education, fertility, mortality, migration and housing and does NOT mention ethnicity or religion, so it is not evidence of a new provincial breakdown.

subnational_sources.title: Muong people (English Wikipedia) -- carries 2019 per-province counts, which implies a published province x ethnic-group table
subnational_sources.publisher: Wikipedia (citing the 2019 census / 2019 survey of 53 ethnic minorities -- citation not seen)
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin1 (2019 geography = 63 provinces; packet draws 64 shapes -- one extra to identify)
subnational_sources.evidence: Search snippet: 'Muong people concentrate in Hoa Binh Province (549,026), Thanh Hoa Province (376,340), Phu Tho Province (218,404), Son La Province (84,676), and Hanoi (62,239)'. Exact five- and six-digit province figures for one ethnic group mean a census-derived province x ethnic-group table has been published somewhere; the article's footnote should name it. The Tay people article snippet likewise lists provinces (Cao Bang, Lang Son, Bac Kan, Thai Nguyen, Quang Ninh, Bac Ninh, Bac Giang) without figures. This is the lead, not the source.

subnational_sources.title: Ket qua toan bo Tong dieu tra dan so va nha o nam 2019 (complete results, Vietnamese-language volume)
subnational_sources.publisher: General Statistics Office of Viet Nam
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin1 if a province cut exists (63 vs 64 shapes)
subnational_sources.evidence: Surfaced for the Vietnamese query on population by religion and province; the snippet only says the census results were released 19 Dec 2019 and that a 26-table compilation exists. The ENGLISH results volume this project already read (docs/SOURCES.md, Viet Nam section) stacks ethnic groups and provinces under one Table 5 caption rather than crossing them, and prints religion only nationally (Table 3). Whether the Vietnamese volume differs is unverified; it is the first thing to read. Vietnamese tables use a space as thousands separator and carry Total/Male/Female (SOURCES.md).

wikipedia.note: The mandated searches ('Religion in Vietnam' by province; 'Ethnic groups in Vietnam' by province; 'Hoang Mai', 'Krong Pac', 'Nghia Hung' Vietnam wikipedia) were refused by the exhausted search budget. Not run, not 'no article'.

tier_reason: Could not establish a provincial publication. The packet's closed route (religion and ethnicity published nationally only) still stands on the evidence gathered; the one new lead is that English Wikipedia ethnic-group articles quote exact 2019 per-province counts, which means a province x ethnic-group table exists somewhere -- but its publisher, URL and format were not located before the search budget ran out.
recommended_action: Three things, in order. (1) Open the Vietnamese 'Ket qua toan bo' PDF (URL above) and look for a province x dan toc (ethnic group) table -- the English volume's Table 5 stacks the two breakdowns, the Vietnamese one may cross them. (2) Read the citation behind the Muong people article's per-province counts; it names the table. (3) Searches still owed: the 2019 census data-exploration portal (tongdieutradanso.vn), the 2019 survey of 53 ethnic minorities (GSO + CEMA) for province-level minority counts, IPUMS-International's Vietnam 2019 sample (registration), and HDX. Geography caveat, unverified this session: Viet Nam reportedly merged its 63 provinces into 34 and abolished the district tier on 1 July 2025; if so, the packet's 64 admin1 / 705 admin2 shapes are the pre-2025 geography, any 2019-census table by 63 provinces still joins to it, and post-2025 publications will not. Confirm before building.

summary: Viet Nam's 2019 census asked ethnicity and religion and the office publishes both only for the whole country, which is what the packet already records; three searches found no provincial religion table and no new publication from the 2024 mid-decade survey. The one new lead is that English Wikipedia's ethnic-group articles quote exact 2019 per-province counts (e.g. Muong: Hoa Binh 549,026), so a province x ethnic-group table has been published somewhere -- most likely in the Vietnamese-language complete-results volume or the 2019 survey of 53 ethnic minorities -- but its URL and format were not located before the session's search budget ran out. Tier D: read the Vietnamese 'Ket qua toan bo' PDF and the Muong article's citation first, then run the owed searches (tongdieutradanso.vn portal, 53-EM survey, IPUMS, HDX). Confirm the reported July 2025 provincial merger before joining anything to the 64-shape admin1 file.
